newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TELECOM FIRM'S Q1 NET PROFIT, INCOME UP.
newsitem.headline: TELECOM FIRM'S Q1 NET PROFIT, INCOME UP.

text.p: Lithuania's state-run phone company, Lithuanian Telecom, said on Friday that its net profit for the first three months of 1997 was 23.06 million litas, up from 12.09 million litas for the same period last year.
The company also said in a statement that its income from communcation services was 144.44 million litas in the first quarter compared to 128.04 million litas in the same period in 1996.

"Our income has increased because since February 1 of this year, subscription fees for phones and rates for international calls have risen," Dzintra Tamuliene, the head of the company's finance department, was quoted as saying in the statement.
She added that for the second quarter, the company hoped that its income would climb to 150 million litas.
The company, which is 100 percent state owned, has been slated for privatisation.
Bids to draw up the phone company's sell-off plan must be submitted by May 9 and the government says it hopes to begin the privatisation process next spring.
The company's share capital currently stands at 75.3 million litas.
